title: Mermaid export for brainstorm-map
summary: Adding a Mermaid export to the existing brainstorm-map skill. Only the parts we touch or depend on are shown — the rest of the skill is deliberately absent.

parts.label: Map JSON
parts.purpose: The map file: themes, nodes, statuses, evidence. Already the single source for both the diagram and the document.
parts.why_here: The export reads it directly, so its shape constrains what a Mermaid graph can express. Nothing about it changes.
open: Mermaid has no equivalent of the status styling — do we encode status in node shape, or lose it?

parts.label: Validator
parts.purpose: Checks ids, labels, statuses and evidence before anything is rendered, and refuses to build on a failure.
parts.why_here: The export must run behind it, not beside it. Exporting an unvalidated map would route around the one gate the skill has.

surface.name: validate
surface.note: Call it first and bail on errs, exactly as main() does. We do not touch it.

surface.name: STATUSES
surface.note: The status vocabulary our Mermaid classDefs have to cover.

parts.label: Build script
parts.purpose: Reads the map JSON, validates it, injects it into the template and writes the HTML.
parts.why_here: This is where the new output format hangs. It gains a flag and a branch; everything else stays.

surface.name: main
surface.note: Default stays html, so every existing invocation behaves identically.
surface.change: Add a --format {html,mermaid,both} argument and branch on it after validation.

surface.name: build
surface.note: Untouched. The Mermaid path is a sibling of this call, not a change to it.

open: Separate .mmd file, or a ```mermaid block appended to a Markdown export?

parts.label: Mermaid writer
parts.purpose: Walks the validated map and emits Mermaid flowchart source: one subgraph per theme, one node per item, classDefs for status.

surface.name: to_mermaid
surface.note: No IO, so it is testable without a repo or a browser.
surface.change: New pure function: map dict in, Mermaid flowchart source out.

open: Node ids in the map contain hyphens, which Mermaid tolerates but some renderers do not — sanitise?
Do excluded nodes come out? The pruning lives in the browser, so the export only sees the file.

parts.label: Viewer template
parts.purpose: The self-contained HTML page: radial map, outline, doc, prune and drag.
parts.why_here: Pruning and dragging only exist in the browser, so a useful export has to be reachable from here too, not just from the command line.

surface.name: clean
surface.note: Already returns the pruned map plus layout. The in-page export feeds on this, not on MAP.

surface.name: renderDoc
surface.note: Reference only — shows the traversal that honours exclusions. We copy the approach, not the code.

open: Copy-to-clipboard only, since downloads are inert inside a published artifact.

parts.label: Skill instructions
parts.purpose: Tells Claude how to run the skill and what the output is.
parts.why_here: A capability nobody is told about does not exist. The workflow section has to mention the flag.

surface.name: Workflow
surface.change: Document the --format flag in the build step and name the .mmd output.
surface.note: A capability nobody is told about does not exist.

edges.label: validates first
edges.note: The export must sit behind the gate, not beside it.

edges.label: same mapping
edges.note: The in-page copy and the CLI output must agree, or two Mermaid dialects appear.
